summary: A 1929 L-4 prototype cab on the Clearwater/Idaho Panhandle boundary, abandoned in the late 1950s and volunteer-restored since 1981.

facts.design: L-4 (one of the 1929 prototype cabs for the design)
facts.status_note: Abandoned as an active lookout; stabilized and maintained by volunteers since 1981, not staffed.

access.note: Hike-in only, no road access; located in the Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area.

visit.trail_note: Foot access only, within a roadless non-motorized trail area.

events.note: First lookout camp established at Mallard Peak, manned by Red Stewart for at least 5 years.
Ground cabin built as one of the prototype cabs leading to the L-4 design.
Other sources give 1957 as decommissioning/abandonment year.
Initial stabilization by Don Mathis, Ray Kresek, and volunteers; Kresek unofficially staffed it that summer.
Inland Empire Llama Association began providing annual maintenance support.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 25, 1996.
Tim Grubham and family did restoration work with USFS approval.

evidence.supports: One of the 1929 prototype cabs for the L-4 design; later L-4s mass-produced in kits for mule delivery
evidence.quote: Mallard Peak Lookout was one of the 1929 prototypes from which the successful L-4 cab evolved (thousands were later produced in prefab kits suitable for delivery by mule packstrings).

evidence.supports: Built by a ranger and crew from Pole Mountain Ranger District, St. Joe National Forest
evidence.quote: It was built by a ranger and his crew on the old Pole Mountain Ranger District of the St. Joe National Forest (both names are now gone and merged into adjacent units).
Located on the boundary between the Clearwater and Idaho Panhandle National Forests within a proposed wilderness, Mallard Peak was last staffed in 1956.

evidence.supports: Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area location between the two Clearwater forks
evidence.quote: Mallard Lookout is located in the Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area, a non motorized trail area that straddles the divide between the North Fork Clearwater River and the Little North Fork Clearwater River basins.

evidence.supports: Martin Peak patrol lookout and 1957 decommissioning
evidence.quote: There was also a patrol lookout 2 1/2 miles away on Martin Peak.
Established as a camp in 1914, a gabled L-4 cab prototype, built in 1929, was abandoned in 1957.

evidence.supports: 1914 camp manned by Red Stewart for 5 years
evidence.quote: A camp was first located here in 1914, with Red Stewart manning the first watch and remaining there for at least 5 years.
In 1981 Ray Kresek and Don Mathis completed the initial stabilization of the structure.
Ray unofficially staffed the lookout that summer.

evidence.supports: Inland Empire Llama Association maintenance since 1992
evidence.quote: Since 1992 the Inland Empire Llama Association has provided annual maintenance.

evidence.supports: 2009 Grubham family restoration with USFS approval
evidence.quote: In 2009 Tim Grubham, along with his family, did restoration work on the lookout with the help and approval of the USFS CdA office and archeologist Sara Wilson.
Mallard Peak Lookout is only accessible by foot and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1956 as the last staffed year; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1957 for abandonment/decommissioning. Both years are noted in the story rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: 1956 vs 1957 last-staffed/abandonment discrepancy left unresolved in the story per guide instructions. NRHP nomination PDF (84001178) not pulled this pass; could firm up build details and exact staffing dates if more budget is available.
